scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A tiny seed becomes a giant tree, and it never eats a single meal. So where does all that food come from?

scenes.name: ingred
scenes.text: Plants make their own food. The recipe needs just three things. Sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide from the air.

scenes.name: water
scenes.text: Roots pull water from the soil, and thin tubes carry it all the way up to the leaves.

scenes.name: air
scenes.text: Carbon dioxide slips in through tiny pores on the leaf, called stomata.

scenes.name: light
scenes.text: Inside leaf cells, chloroplasts hold chlorophyll. It soaks up red and blue light, and bounces green back. That's why leaves look green.

scenes.name: split
scenes.text: That light energy splits water. The oxygen floats out as waste. The air we breathe.

scenes.name: sugar
scenes.text: The captured energy then joins carbon dioxide into glucose, a sugar the plant uses to grow and live.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Light, water, air, sugar. Breakfast made from sunshine. Follow for more on how things really work.
